title: Eternity and the productions of time

data.source: A pile of 500 seeded occasions (Phoenix study ETERNITY-AND-FINITUDE-2026-10-06, checks 3a to 3d), and that study's stored figures for three clocks. The proverbs are from William Blake, The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, plate 7 (public domain).
data.licence: public domain (Blake); none needed for the toy

prediction: Nothing in the world is predicted. As arithmetic: a pile of finished moments only grows, is finite at every Now, fixes the present without help from anything later, and can take any length of clock time.
baseline: The philosophers Phoenix sets the sentence beside, in their own words (Boethius, Augustine, Spinoza, Whitehead), and the block-universe and plain-forecast readings of time, which fit every experiment run so far equally well.
why: The arithmetic holds and gives the owner's reading of Blake an exact referent: the finite, growing pile of what has been settled. Phoenix records that this reading is coherent, has Whitehead for an ancestor, and "cannot be raised to evidence". A proverb that fits is not a result.
phoenix_status: ONTOLOGY (commitments M1 and M7). "These are philosophical framing, not evidence." "Layer: metaphysics"; "Rung: none". Register row ND-1 (Growing Block against eternalism against plain forecast): NOT DECIDABLE, breaking intervention "none known". Phoenix: "it cannot be raised to evidence".
